properties.program:
# Animation tab: frames 40, play-mode loop
# inputs: lam (wavelength), d (slit separation)
view 0, -58, 140, 45
k = 2 * pi / lam
w = 2 * pi * t
b = 30
s = 128

# the wave coming in from the left: straight crests marching right
field 0, -45, b, 90, 60, 180, 0.5 + 0.5 * cos(k * x - w)  with color "#7fdbff"

# past the barrier: a circular wave from each slit, the two added --
# cos a + cos b = 2 cos((a + b) / 2) cos((a - b) / 2), so the water
# swings at the mean path and is calm wherever the paths differ by an
# odd number of half wavelengths
field b, -45, s - b, 90, 196, 180,
      0.5 + 0.5 * cos(k * (b + (hypot(x - b, y - d / 2) + hypot(x - b, y + d / 2)) / 2) - w) * cos(k * (hypot(x - b, y - d / 2) - hypot(x - b, y + d / 2)) / 2)  with color "#7fdbff"

# the screen: how bright each point gets on average, cos^2 of half the
# phase difference between the two paths
field s, -45, 140 - s, 90, 1, 180,
      pow(cos(k * (hypot(x - b, y - d / 2) - hypot(x - b, y + d / 2)) / 2), 2)  with color "#ffd700"

# the barrier, with its two slits 2 wide
with fill "#9a9a9a", color "#9a9a9a"
    rect b - 1, -45, 2, 45 - d / 2 - 1
    rect b - 1, -d / 2 + 1, 2, d - 2
    rect b - 1, d / 2 + 1, 2, 45 - d / 2 - 1
end

with color "#c8d8e8", font 4.5
    text 2, -51.5, "wavelength %.0f", lam  with align "left"
    text 79, -51.5, "slits %.0f apart", d
    text 138, -51.5, "screen"  with align "right"
end

properties.text: THE DOUBLE-SLIT EXPERIMENT, seen from above like a ripple tank.  Straight waves come in from the left and pass through two slits in a barrier; a circular wave spreads from each slit, and where they meet they add.  Where a crest of one meets a trough of the other the water stays calm: those are the still lines fanning out from between the slits.  The gold strip on the right is the screen -- how bright each point of it gets on average -- and its bright bands are the interference fringes.  Spin the wheel over the knobs: a longer WAVELENGTH spreads the fringes apart, a wider SLIT SEPARATION crowds them together (their spacing on the screen is about wavelength x distance / separation).  Every shade is drawn with the Figure's field statement, which colours a grid of cells from an expression of each cell's x and y -- here some 70,000 cells a frame.  Open the Figure (double-click) to see the program.
